In this case, a claim application/ petition u/s 166 MV Act was filed by claimant/ petitioner.

2. As per the allegation of the claimant in such claim petition, in the morning at about 07.00 AM on 19.04.2015, such claimant/ petitioner along with one Manikant Mishra was going for morning walk at Sec. 37, Faridabad, Haryana.

When they reached near mother dairy of such sec. 37, a motorcycle bearing no. DL 3SBV 4856 being driven by driver in a rash and negligent manner and a very high speed came from opposite side, which was driven by R- 1 and hit the claimant and his friend Mani Kant.
As a result, they fell on the road and got injured due to forceful impact by offending vehicle.
It is further claimed that such claimant sustained multiple grievous injury.
He was removed to Sarvodaya Hospital, Sect. 19, Faridabad, Haryana and remained hospitalized there from 19.04.2015 to 22.04.2015.
It is further stated that such offending vehicle is owned by R-2 and insured by R-3.
Further a compensation of Rs. 8 lakhs is demanded in the present claim petition along with interest @ 12% per annum from the date of filing.
3. It is further claimed that FIR in question got registered by concerned police official u/s 279, 337 IPC.
It is further stated that ultimately charge sheet u/s 279, 337, 338 IPC r/w Sec. 3/181 MV Act filed against such minor/ R-1 on MACT No.: 3749/16 Surender Singh Vs Chandan & ors.

5. Further as per record, such R-1 & R-2 did not file any reply and did not contested the present claim petition.
6. But reply/ report filed by insurance company/R-3 dated 09.09.2016.

In nutshell, in such reply, it is stated that insurance company that R-1/ alleged driver has been acquitted by trial court/ JJB on account of lack of evidence at the statement of alleged eye witness Mani Kant and injured / present claimant Surender Singh did not supported the prosecution and both of them categorically stated that R-1 is not involved in the occurrence of present accident.
As such, it is further stated that as there is acquittal of driver from criminal charge, no claim under present petition is made out.
It is further stated that claimant has suppressed material facts/ documents.

It is further stated that in case, driver and owner do not contest present petition, under section 170 MV Act, insurance company be given liberty to take all defences available to such driver and owner but it is not denied that alleged offending vehicle in question is insured by R-3.

24. But on going through the record of the connected criminal case, it can be noted that such connected criminal case record, despite opportunity available and directions given by this Tribunal not filed by the claimant side.
In any case, it is only opposite side/ insurance company witness R3W1 who proved on record the same.
As per such copy of charge sheet and documents annexed therewith there is a statement of Mani Kant Mishra based on which FIR in question was registered.
Further there is site plan prepared by IO regarding the spot of accident as well as mechanical inspection report dated 22.07.2015.
Further a copy of charge sheet is also placed on record in which such R-1 is charged with offences as mentioned above.
25. But thereafter, there is a copy of order by concerned Juvenile Justice Board, Faridabad dated 04.12.2015 in criminal case no. 102, instituted on 21.08.2015.
In such order which is not disputed by any party, also the filing of such Criminal case against R-1 is noted.
It is further mentioned that as such, "notice" was served upon such R-1 and he pleaded not guilty and claimed inquiry.

It is further stated that present claimant Mr. Surender Singh was examined in that proceeding before ld. JJB Board and it can be noted from para no. 10 & 11 of such judgment, as also argued by Ld. Counsel for insurance company, that Such claimant Mr. Surender Singh stated that R-1 is not involved in the accident in question.
As such, such Mr. Surender Singh was declared hostile before Ld. JJB.
During his cross examination by Ld. APP also, he stated that he did not name such R-1/ Juvenile in question.
He further deposed that he did not know the juvenile and never seen him before.
26. Thus, it is clear, which is not uncommon, that claimants like the present MACT No.: 3749/16 Surender Singh Vs Chandan & ors.

sentences.text: Page No. 7 of 15 rpt Mr. Surender Singh are taking complete contrary stand in criminal proceedings viz a viz in claim petition in MACT.
In the present case, it is clear that in order to shield such R-1, claimant Surender Singh deposed to the contrary that such R-1 is not involved in the accident.

Whereas in the present claim petition, to make out a case, taking a u-turn, he deposed that accident is caused by such R- 1.
27.

It may further be noted that such claimant tried to suppress such material fact before this claim Tribunal and did not produce copy of such criminal record nor stated in his evidence before this Tribunal on 20.05.2017 in his examination in chief by way of affidavit that he has already denied the involvement of R-1 in the accident in question.

It may further be noted that this Tribunal is aware about the aspect that in a criminal case and inquiry before Tribunal, standard of proof is different.
Much higher standard is required of the level of beyond reasonable doubt in case of criminal trial.
Whereas, as already noted above, standard of proof required in present matter is even below preponderance of probability.

29. But it may further be noted that it is not the case where because of different standard of proof in a criminal case viz a viz in a claim petition of present nature, that two different findings are given by the concerned criminal side court/ JJB and this MACT.

But rather, it is a case, where because of contrary, false and malafied stand taken by the claimant/ injured/ witness Mr. Surender Singh himself, a different finding of acquittal is arrived by concerned Ld. JJB regarding non involvement of such R-1 as driver of the offending vehicle in question.

30. But having observed and held so regarding the conduct of claimant Surender Singh, it is further noted that an independent separate finding need to be given as far as present claim petition is concerned.
MACT No.: 3749/16 Surender Singh Vs Chandan & ors.
Page No. 8 of 15 rpt 31.

In this background, it may further be noted that in any case, as far as present claim petition is concerned, from the material on record, including the criminal case record, charge sheet against the R-1 and non appearance of such R-1 & 2 in the present case and evidence of PW-1/ Mr. Surender Singh, having regard to the standard of proof in a MACT case, it is held that R-1 was present at the spot of accident.
Further, it is R-1 who caused the accident and injury to the claimant in question by the offending vehicle/ motorcycle in question by driving the same in rash and negligent manner.

32. Further, although, it is already observed above, in order to illegally and malafiedly support the R-1 & 2, the R-1 deposed falsely before the concerned Ld. JJB but, it is further held that claimant suffered injury in question in the accident in question.
33. The issue No.1 is decided accordingly, in favour of the petitioner.

A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

35. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary damages (Special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
35.1.

In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a)
and (iv).
35.2.

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of MACT No.: 3749/16 Surender Singh Vs Chandan & ors. Page No. 10 of 15 rpt amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 35.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence.
35.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof.

35.5. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)-- involves determination of l u m p s u m a m o u n t s w i t h r e f e r e n c e t o c i r c u m s t a n c e s s u c h a s a g e , n a t u r e o f Surender Singh vs . Chandan & Ors.
